prize_parts.citation: For developing targeted protein degradation, in which designed small molecules recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to destroy chosen proteins.

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation meets the standard I hold: a simple, almost modest chemical idea, a bifunctional molecule or a glue that brings a target to an E3 ligase, that opened a part of the proteome once called undruggable and has already shown real consequences in many clinical programmes. The 2001 PROTAC concept of Crews and Deshaies, followed by the mechanistic identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target by Handa, gives a coherent story that connects a mechanism, a design principle and a drug class. It has had more than two decades of independent validation, and it is chemistry in the sense that matters: control of molecular recognition and of ternary-complex equilibria. Having heard colleagues, I still rank it first. It has the broadest support across the committee outside the base-editing camp, with rankings from Aili, Chabes, Brzezinski, Somfai and Sparr.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that the field is not one discovery but two lineages, PROTACs and molecular glues, and three seats cannot honestly cover Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli, Handa, Ito, Sakamoto, Gray and Kim. Any three-person cut will look arbitrary to someone. Approved PROTAC drugs remain few, so a sceptic can say the clinical consequence is still promissory, and the medicinal chemistry is largely modular. If the committee decides the prize should be one coherent lineage, the glue and cereblon strand sits awkwardly with the 2001 PROTAC paper.

responses.point: Somfai ranks degraders fifth, accepting the proximity-induction design concept but doubting the underlying chemistry is more than modular medicinal chemistry, and he substitutes Ciulli for Handa.
responses.response: I accept that the coupling chemistry is modular, but I would not hold that against it: the Nobel tradition I value, such as click chemistry in 2022, rewards simple ideas that make functional molecules easy to build. The novelty is the design principle, and the cereblon mechanism is real chemistry, not packaging. On Ciulli, his VHL ligand and ternary-complex structural work is important, but it refines a concept that Crews and Deshaies already established. Handa explains why thalidomide and its analogues work, which is a distinct discovery. I would keep Handa over Ciulli, though I recognise that this is the weakest seat in my configuration.

responses.point: Chabes ranks base editing first and degraders second, regarding base editing as deaminase chemistry applied to one nucleotide, with Liu, Komor and Gaudelli credited as the decisive contributors.
responses.response: I agree that base editing is chemically designed and clinically consequential, and I ranked it fourth, so we are not far apart. My disagreement is about maturity and framing. It dates from 2016 and 2017, patient evidence is early, and it follows the 2020 CRISPR prize closely, so a committee could fairly see it as a refinement of a tool already honoured. I would also challenge the assumption that Komor and Gaudelli belong in the prize, since trainees rarely receive recognition when the leader is the natural single laureate, which weakens the three-name configuration. Degraders have a longer record and a cleaner mechanistic case.

responses.point: Brzezinski places degraders fifth, behind Gray and Winkler on electron transfer and serial femtosecond crystallography, and his configuration puts Ciulli in place of Deshaies, asking whether clinical validation is sufficient.
responses.response: I respect the physical rigour of the Gray and Winkler work, but it extends the Marcus theory prize and leaves a smaller set of consequences than a new drug modality. On clinical validation I share your worry and said so in my opening; still, the committee has often rewarded a concept before its drug count is large, and many degraders are in late-stage trials. I would not drop Deshaies. He co-authored the first PROTAC paper with Crews, and the priority question cannot be settled by dropping him, whereas Ciulli's contribution came later.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, ranks base editing first and massively parallel sequencing second, and he wonders whether base and prime editing might be treated together.
responses.response: I would resist combining base and prime editing, because the two share the fusion of an editing enzyme to Cas9 but have different chemistry, and prime editing is too recent to judge. I also doubt that sequencing, which you rank second, is a better fit. Its credit is divided among Solexa, 454 and Lynx strands, and the committee would be choosing between companies as much as people. Degraders have a more tractable attribution problem.

uncertainties: Whether the prize should be a single PROTAC-and-glue lineage or whether glues deserve separate recognition, and whether Handa or Ciulli takes the third seat.
Whether the current clinical record of degraders, with few approved drugs, is enough to count as demonstrated consequence.
Whether base editing is judged to be chemistry rather than medicine, and how heavily the 2020 CRISPR prize weighs against it.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile. None of the candidates I discuss is connected to my Warshel and EVB postdoc network, the Uppsala ribosome community or my free-energy work.
